newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end lower on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Thursday in a moderate session, pressured by forecasts for more moderate weather next week but prices held technical support, industry sources said.
February slumped 27 cents to close at $3.341 per million British thermal units. March settled 23.6 cents lower at $2.909. Others ended down by 1.8 to 15 cents.

"When you're trading cash in the $4.60 and $4.70 area, it's tough to be a big seller of Feb at $3.30. On Monday, we could be looking at another Arctic front,"said an East Coast trader, referring to forecasts for more Arctic air later next week.

He was referring to a forecast released late Wednesday by Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis calling for another Arctic blast by the weekend of January 25. Davis said a cold pattern above Hudson Bay in Canada known as the Hudson Bay vortex will likely persist for a minimum of a few weeks, bringing more cold to the Midwest and Northeast.
But traders said near-term forecasts calling for some moderation in temperatures early next week helped trigger today's selloff.
Most agreed weather remains the key, meaning the only certainty will be more volatility based on the most recent forecast.

Technical traders noted February twice tested and held support Thursday in the $3.30 area. They pegged next support in the gap between $3.11 and $3.185. Resistance was seen at $3.64 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area.

Cash prices at the Gulf Coast jumped almost 40 cents Thursday to near $4.70. Midcon pipes tumbled almost 40 cents to the $4.80 area on forecasts for more moderate temperatures this weekend. Gas at the New York city gate was talked in the $6.00-6.50 area, up more than $1 on the day.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 9.3 cents to $2.436. NYMEX said an estimated 39,953 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 47,536.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, February closed 25 cents lower at $3.15, while deferred months finished down by two to 22 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by two cents to 19.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 337 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's total of 293.
